title: Interleaved tensor suspension with its internal differential
statement:
Use smallness as in [def-weil-size-convention], tensor products as in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and cochain shifts as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $K[r]^q=K^{q+r}$ and $d_{K[r]}=(-1)^r d_K$. For $n\geq0$ let $K_0,\ldots,K_{n+1}$ be arbitrary cochain complexes of abelian groups. Let $E=\mathbf Z\varepsilon$ in degree $-1$ with zero differential. Put $V_n=K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n+1}$ and $W_n=K_0\otimes E\otimes K_1\otimes E\otimes\cdots\otimes K_n\otimes E\otimes K_{n+1}$, with the tensor differential $d(u\otimes v)=du\otimes v+(-1)^{|u|}u\otimes dv$ and direct-sum totalization. For homogeneous $x=a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{n+1}$, the formula
$$\Phi_n(x)=(-1)^{\alpha_n(x)}a_0\otimes\varepsilon\otimes a_1\otimes\varepsilon\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n\otimes\varepsilon\otimes a_{n+1},\qquad \alpha_n(x)=n+\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(n+1-j)|a_j|$$
defines an isomorphism of cochain complexes $\Phi_n:V_n[n+1]\xrightarrow{\sim}W_n$, natural in degree-zero chain maps of all $K_j$. In particular $d_{W_n}\Phi_n=\Phi_n((-1)^{n+1}d_{V_n})$. The same formula defines the inverse by removing the generators and multiplying by the same sign; no flatness or boundedness of the $K_j$ is required.

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, section 3.1, equations (3.1)-(3.2), and section 3.6(i); agent-explicit sign identification for the interleaved tensor complexes in that construction. No Stacks tag states this sign-normalized arbitrary-length comparison.

proof.text: Fix n and write |a_j| for the degree of a homogeneous pure tensor factor. Since E is the free abelian group on one generator ε in degree -1, the universal property of the tensor product gives a unique multilinear map sending a_0⊗⋯⊗a_{n+1} to the displayed interleaved tensor. Its degree is Σ_j|a_j|−(n+1), which is the degree of x in V_n[n+1], because the shift is K[r]^q=K^{q+r}. Multiplication by the integer sign (-1)^{α_n(x)} therefore defines a homogeneous degree-zero map Φ_n on pure tensors and hence on V_n[n+1]. The construction uses only the stated tensor products and the fixed generator ε.

source.place: Drinfeld, §§3.1 and 3.6(i), with the sign identification written out here

proof.text: Define Ψ_n on a homogeneous interleaved pure tensor by removing the ε factors and multiplying by the same sign (-1)^{α_n}, where α_n is computed from the remaining a_j. The tensor universal property makes Ψ_n well defined and additive. On every homogeneous pure tensor, Ψ_nΦ_n and Φ_nΨ_n multiply by (-1)^{2α_n}=1, so they are inverse maps. A degree-zero chain map on each K_j preserves every |a_j| and commutes with the multilinear tensor maps; consequently it commutes with Φ_n and Ψ_n. Thus the maps are natural in all K_j before the differential identity is checked.

source.place: Drinfeld, §3.1, word decomposition and §3.6(i), sign-normalized identification

proof.text: It remains to compare differentials. In the W_n tensor differential, the term differentiating a_j has the Koszul exponent Σ_{k<j}|a_k|−j, because j copies of ε, each of degree −1, precede a_j. Hence its coefficient after Φ_n is (-1)^{α_n+Σ_{k<j}|a_k|−j}. In d_{V_n} the same term has exponent Σ_{k<j}|a_k|. After applying the shift differential (-1)^{n+1} and then Φ_n to the tensor with a_j replaced by da_j, the exponent is n+1+Σ_{k<j}|a_k|+α_n+(n+1−j), since |da_j|=|a_j|+1. These two exponents differ by 2n+2, so the coefficients agree. Summing over j gives d_{W_n}Φ_n=Φ_n((-1)^{n+1}d_{V_n}); d^2=0 and the tensor Leibniz rule give no additional terms because dε=0.

source.place: Drinfeld, §§3.1 and 3.6(i), internal differential sign calculation

proof.text: The argument includes n=0: there is one ε, α_0=|a_0|, and the same exponent calculation gives the shift sign (-1). It also includes homogeneous elements of arbitrary degree and unbounded complexes, since each equality is checked on finite pure tensors and then extended additively; no truncation, boundedness, or flatness is invoked. Therefore Φ_n is a natural isomorphism of cochain complexes with the stated inverse and differential formula.
